newsitem.title: CHINA: China not to build new oil refineries before 2000.
newsitem.headline: China not to build new oil refineries before 2000.

text.p: State-owned China National Petroleum Corp (Sinopec) will not build new oil refineries for at least three years but will focus on expanding output of existing plants, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
More oil refineries should follow the example of the Zhenhai refinery which was working to double its capacity and cut costs, Xinhua quoted Sheng Huaren, president of Sinopec, as saying.

"Domestic petrochemical enterprises have to increase economic efficiency and enhance their competitiveness since more and more foreign companies have entered China and made market competition even more fierce," Sheng said.

"We will upgrade our existing enterprises through overall technological renovation, rather than launching new projects in the next three years or even early in the next century," Xinhua quoted Sheng as saying.
Sheng's comments repeated earlier statements by Chinese oil officials that no new oil refineries were planned before the beginning of next century.
The ban on new refinery projects would help Sinopec cut total investment in the 1996-2000 period to 150 billion yuan ($18 billion) from the previously planned 180 billion yuan, Sheng said.

Hong Kong-listed Zhenhai Refining & Chemical Co in the eastern province of Zhejiang, had set a good example for the refining sector with its cost-cutting reforms and programme to boost output, he said.
"Expanding production capacity of old enterprises through intensive technological renovation has been proved more economical and efficient than building new ones," he said.
Zhenhai was working to double its refining capacity through technological upgrades, he said.
"Zhenhai will be a model of not only the refinery industry, but also other petrochemical sectors such as deep processing of petroleum, chemical fiber and chemical fertilizer production," he said.
Sinopec was also looking for foreign partners to set up large petrochemical joint ventures, he said.

"We are negotiating with some big foreign firms and planning to join hands in establishing 600,000-tonne ethylene projects at Nanjing, Shanghai, Lanzhou and Tianjin cities and in Fujian province," he said but gave no further details.
China processed 118 million tonnes of crude oil and produced 2.45 million tonnes of ethylene in 1996, Xinhua said.
